description: meta.json is fetched TWICE (two separate `curl -sSf`, lines 19 and 20). If the first succeeds and the second transiently fails, AKASH_NODE becomes empty and the guard on line 22 fail-closes — acceptable, but wasteful and creates a TOCTOU where chain_id and node could come from two different fetches (e.g. if the file changes between calls or one curl hits a different CDN edge). Also `curl ... | jq -r '.apis.rpc[0].address'` assumes the FIRST rpc endpoint is healthy; no fallback to rpc[1..]. A single dead rpc[0] takes down every spawn. The meta.json fetch-fail edge (spec EDGE CASES) IS handled (line 22 guard) so that requirement passes, but robustness is weak.

evidence.snippet:
export AKASH_CHAIN_ID="...$(curl -sSf "$META" | jq -r '.chain_id')"
export AKASH_NODE="...$(curl -sSf "$META" | jq -r '.apis.rpc[0].address')"

correctFix: Fetch meta.json ONCE into a var, then jq both fields out of it. Consider trying rpc[0..N] until one answers a quick `status` query before committing to it.
